summary: #126: nostr-tools leaves the plugin's declared dependencies (now a devDependency, still installed by npm install --include=dev) and is loaded only when a Nostr route runs, through a computed require. OpenClaw copies every declared plugin dependency file by file on the Gateway main thread at the first owner turn after each restart; the declared set drops from 635 files (nostr-tools and its @noble/@scure tree: 616) to ws alone (19).
reason: S24 CPU profile of 01/11 12:56 (Gateway restarted on purpose): the first owner turn held the main thread ~90 s (eventLoopDelayMax 46.6 s, WhatsApp closed in 408, run start 91 s after the request). 44.2 s sat under loadInstalledSessionStoreSdk's first import, of which capturePluginDependencies 27.4 s and verifyPluginSourceInputs 13.9 s, dominated by lstat/read/open on those dependency files. 16 of the 17 Gateway stalls of 31/10 were this first turn. Nostr had no activity in the day's logs.

capabilities.reason: No capability, route or tool changes; the Nostr routes keep their behaviour and load their library on first use.

architecture.reason: Package metadata and one lazy require in the existing Nostr owner. No new store, router, scheduler, daemon or retry.

evidence: Plugin dependency metadata and a lazy require; no MCP tool, schema or adapter change.

limitations: Measured cost left after this change: the lazy agent-runtime plugin registry (loadOpenClawPlugins, ~15 s, OpenClaw) and the verification of the remaining captured files; to be measured on the S24 after deployment with the same restart profile.
The first Nostr call after a restart now pays that library's capture once (only when Nostr is used).
